newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Asia said world's top sugar producer and consumer.
newsitem.headline: Asia said world's top sugar producer and consumer.

text.p: Fast-growing Asia is both the world's top sugar-producing and consuming region, with growth being led by India and Malaysia, an industry official said on Tuesday.

Peter Baron, executive director of the International Sugar Organisation (ISO), told a sugar conference on the tourist island of Bali that Asian sugar output reached 37.1 million tonnes in 1995, representing 32 percent of the world total.
"When it comes to consumption, here too Asia leads the world. The Asian consumption in 1995 amounted to 43.29 million tonnes or 38 percent of the world total," he added.
Baron said per capita consumption in the region was only 12.7 kgs compared to the world average of 20 kgs.
"Obviously there remains a large potential for increase in Asia, especially noting that per capita consumption in China is only six kgs," he said.
He said the main growth markets in Asia are India, Malaysia, South Korea and Indonesia. He did not give details on these countries' consumption patterns.
Baron said consumption growth in Asia had a decisive effect on imports. In 1995, Asia imported 14.76 million tonnes, representing 42.5 percent of the world total.
"The growth in imports since 1989 has been a massive 4.96 million tonnes, or 51 percent, with a breath-taking annual growth of 8.5 percent," he said.
"Mainly responsible for this dynamic growth were the rapidly developing economies of the Pacific Rim, especially Malaysia, Korea, China and also Indonesia," he added.

He said Asian sugar exports reached 6.28 million tonnes or 18 percent of world exports in 1995, adding that the impressive annual growth rate of 7.2 percent between 1990-95 could be attributed mainly to Thailand.
"In aggregate, Asia is clearly the biggest producing and consuming continent with the largest sugar trade turnover."
